text.p: The central bank again provided banks with sizeable amounts of funds on Thursday as the liquidity squeeze eased slightly, bankers said.
The bank lent 11.8 trillion lira of overnight money to the cash-stripped banks at 75 percent and fed 8.1 trillion lira via seven-day repos at an average rate of 74.23 percent.

It had injected a total of 55.9 trillion lira via overnight funding and a repo auction on Wednesday. The central bank lowered the average repo rate to 74.23 percent today from Wednesday's 74.34 as the cash shortage diminished.

The lira weakened sharply to 91,250 to the dollar from Wednesday's 90,720 close because of a firmer dollar/mark parity, but its downside was limited by ongoing cash demand, which curbed demand for the U.S. currency.

The central bank also raised its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers gradually to 91,300 lira from 90,700 at Wednesday's close, in line with the dollar's gains in international markets.
T-bill yields eased around one point on expectations that cash demand might ease in coming days after central bank funding decreased from the level of the last few days.
The average yield on the most active April 9, 1997 paper fell to 127.92 percent from yesterday's 128.41 percent.
The second most heavily traded March 26, 1997 yielded 127.41 percent after 128 percent on Wednesday. -- Istanbul newsroom +90-212-275 08 75
